name: FINDR fire and security observation guide
scope: General observation guides for fire, intruder, access control, CCTV and warden-call systems. Source examples are model-specific; no model-specific repair procedure is inferred from a picture or downloaded manual.
rankingNotice: Ranked possibilities based on your answers, not a confirmed diagnosis. Editorial weights have not been calibrated against real fault data.
weightMeaning: P(yes | cause) is a design heuristic only. It is not manufacturer reliability data or a measured probability.
unresolvedNotice: Fault not identified. Keep the observations and refer to the exact-model manual or technical support.
safety: For a fire condition or suspected fire, follow the site emergency procedure. These questions collect observations; any electrical work or impairment requires the site procedure and a competent engineer.

engineGuidance.prior: Equal within the chosen symptom group. Never describe equal priors as prevalence.
engineGuidance.questionChoice: Choose the unanswered question with the greatest expected information gain under current relative weights. Tie-break deterministically.
engineGuidance.update: Yes multiplies by p; No by 1-p. I don’t know makes no change to candidate weights. Recompute from original answers when undoing an answer. Only valid answers to questions in the selected group count as evidence.
engineGuidance.stopping: At most all available questions. Permit early viewing and continued questioning. If all answers are unknown or no positive distinguishing evidence exists, show unresolved rather than best guess.
engineGuidance.display: Show up to three possibilities with the matching observations and source references. Do not display probability percentages or say fixed/safe/confirmed.
engineGuidance.multipleFaults: The model considers one symptom group at a time. Multiple simultaneous faults can have different causes. An unknown/out-of-scope outcome must always be available.
engineGuidance.legacyAnswers: Older saved Probably / Probably not answers retain their original half-strength weight and are labelled as earlier-session answers. They are not offered in new questions and are never silently strengthened into Yes / No.
